analysis:
This PR only modifies docs/architecture/inference.md. The patch updates the last-updated date and the documented Nemotron Super encoded media body ceiling, from 8 MiB to 40 MiB. It also changes the over-limit error from invalid-media 400 to media_too_large. No code, configuration, crypto, attestation, or authorization logic changes in the supplied evidence. The two assigned units are base_text excerpts (lines 1611-2365) that fall outside the changed ranges (base 3, 128-130, 540-541). I read them and found no change to the security-relevant behavior they describe: MiMo media accounting, prefix-cache and SSD checkpoint contracts, tool parsers, reasoning seeds, and the invariants/failure-mode tables.

One point for integration. The documented raise of NemotronSuperServingPolicy.maximumEncodedBodyBytes to 40 MiB widens the memory and DoS surface (T-010, TB-007). The documentation states that the media-charge reservation against the shared budget (503 on failure), the owner lock, and the per-request 429 for concurrent image requests still apply before allocation. The code that implements this (NemotronSuperServingPolicy) is not in the supplied batch. I cannot verify that the 40 MiB limit is enforced before base64 decode or buffering. The doc change is therefore not evidence of a regression, but the implementing PR's source, if any, should be checked for the pre-allocation size gate. No threat-model entries need updating from the doc text alone. T-041 (prefix cache) is unaffected.
